request.description:
This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of police stations.

### Request

The request does not require any parameters.

### Response

The response will have a status code of 200 and a content type of `application/json`. The body of the response will contain an array of objects, each representing a police station. Each object will have the following properties:

- `facility_name`: The name of the police station facility
    
- `formatted_address`: The formatted address of the police station
    
- `id`: The unique identifier of the police station
    
- `latitude`: The latitude coordinate of the police station location
    
- `longitude`: The longitude coordinate of the police station location
    
- `postcode`: The postcode of the police station location
    
- `suburb`: The suburb of the police station location
    

#### Sample Response:

``` json
[
    {
        "facility_name": "BRANXHOLME POLICE STATION",
        "formatted_address": "87-89 MONROE STREET",
        "id": 1,
        "latitude": -37.858419148,
        "longitude": 141.798754529,
        "postcode": "3302",
        "suburb": "Branxholme"
    }
]

 ```

request.description:
### Get Self Defense Centers

This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve a list of self-defense centers.

#### Request Body

This request does not require a request body.

#### Response

- Status: 200 OK
    
- Content-Type: application/json
    

The response body will contain an array of objects, each representing a self-defense center. Each object includes the following properties:

- `id` (number): The unique identifier of the center.
    
- `academy_name` (string): The name of the self-defense academy.
    
- `address` (string): The address of the center.
    
- `contact` (string): The contact information for the center.
    
- `type` (string): The type of the self-defense center.
    
- `website` (string): The website of the center.
    

Example Response:

``` json
[
    {
        "academy_name": "Dynamite Muay Thai ",
        "address": "Level 1/388 Bourke St, Melbourne VIC 3000",
        "contact": "0433 568 256",
        "id": 1,
        "type": "Muay Thai",
        "website": "http://www.dynamitemuaythai.com/"
    }
]

 ```

request.description:
### Get Pedestrian Count by Period

This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve pedestrian count data. The response is in JSON format and includes the following fields:

- days_covered: The number of days covered by the data.
    
- hours_covered: The number of hours covered by the data.
    
- id: The unique identifier for the pedestrian count data.
    
- latitude: The latitude coordinate of the location.
    
- location_id: The unique identifier for the location.
    
- longitude: The longitude coordinate of the location.
    
- period_of_time: The time period for which the data is collected.
    
- postcode: The postal code of the location.
    
- sensor_description: Description of the pedestrian sensor.
    
- sensor_name: Name of the pedestrian sensor.
    
- suburb: The suburb where the pedestrian count is recorded.
    
- total_pedestrian_count: The total count of pedestrians recorded.
    

This information provides a comprehensive overview of the pedestrian count data retrieved from the specified location.

This API endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve pedestrian count data.

### Sample Response

``` json
[
    {
        "days_covered": 355.0,
        "hours_covered": 2124,
        "id": 1,
        "latitude": -37.81349441,
        "location_id": 1,
        "longitude": 144.96515323,
        "period_of_time": "1. Late Night (12am-6am)",
        "postcode": "3000",
        "sensor_description": "Bourke Street Mall (North)",
        "sensor_name": "Bou292_T",
        "suburb": "Melbourne",
        "total_pedestrian_count": 85536
    }
]

 ```

This endpoint is used to retrieve pedestrian count data.

request.description:
# Retrieve Crime Data

This endpoint makes an HTTP GET request to retrieve crime data from the server.

### Response

The response will be in JSON format with the following fields:

- `id` (number): The unique identifier for the crime incident.
    
- `incidents_recorded` (number): The number of incidents recorded for the crime.
    
- `lat` (number): The latitude coordinate of the crime location.
    
- `local_government_area` (string): The local government area where the crime occurred.
    
- `lon` (number): The longitude coordinate of the crime location.
    
- `offence_count` (number): The count of the specific type of offence.
    
- `offence_division` (string): The division of the offence.
    
- `offence_subdivision` (string): The subdivision of the offence.
    
- `offence_subgroup` (string): The subgroup of the offence.
    
- `postcode` (string): The postcode of the crime location.
    
- `suburb_town_name` (string): The name of the suburb or town where the crime occurred.
    
- `year` (number): The year in which the crime occurred.
    

This API endpoint allows users to retrieve crime data.

## Request

### HTTP Request

`GET http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/crime`

## Response

- Status: 200
    
- Content-Type: application/json
    

Example Response Body:

``` json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "incidents_recorded": 1.0,
        "lat": null,
        "local_government_area": "Melbourne",
        "lon": null,
        "offence_count": 1.0,
        "offence_division": "A Crimes against the person",
        "offence_subdivision": "A20 Assault and related offences",
        "offence_subgroup": "A232 Non-FV Common assault",
        "postcode": "3000",
        "suburb_town_name": "Carlton",
        "year": 2024
    }
]

 ```

request.description:
# Victims API

This API endpoint retrieves information about victims of various offenses.

## Request

### Endpoint

`GET /api/victims`

### Response

#### Status: 200 OK

#### Content-Type: application/json

The response body contains an array of victim objects, each containing the following properties:

- `id` (number): The unique identifier for the victim record.
    
- `offence_division` (string): The division of the offense.
    
- `offence_subdivision` (string): The subdivision of the offense.
    
- `sex` (string): The gender of the victim.
    
- `total_victims` (number): The total number of victims.
    
- `victims` (number): The specific number of victims.
    
- `year` (number): The year of the victim record.
    

### Response

The response will be in JSON format with the following schema:

``` json
[
    {
        "id": 1,
        "offence_division": "A Crimes against the person",
        "offence_subdivision": "A10 Homicide and related offences",
        "sex": "Females",
        "total_victims": 226,
        "victims": 76,
        "year": 2024
    }
]

 ```
